question: What is the SI unit of momentum?
solution:
The correct answer is __**kg m s⁻¹**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Momentum** is a fundamental concept in **physics** that describes the quantity of motion an object has.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• The formula for momentum (**p**) is given by **p = m × v**, where **m** is the mass of the object and **v** is its velocity.
 
• The **SI unit** (International System of Units) for mass is **kilogram (kg)** and for velocity is **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
• Therefore, the SI unit of momentum is derived from these two units, resulting in **kg m s⁻¹**.
 
• Understanding momentum is crucial in various fields of **physics** and **engineering**, such as in the study of collisions and conservation laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹**__

 __
 
• This unit is used in the context of viscosity in fluid dynamics, specifically the **dynamic viscosity**.
 
• Dynamic viscosity is a measure of a fluid's resistance to flow.
 
 
 
• **kg m**__
 __
 
• This combination of units does not correspond to a standard physical quantity in the SI system.
 
 
 
• **kg m s**__
 
 
• This unit is incorrect because it does not account for the squared time unit required for velocity.
